1 Year of Battlefield 6 

Imo, failed reinvention of the wheel yet again, feels just as bad as BF2042 was and traditionally bad with the updates & bug fixes. 

Gunplay: The most schizophrenic gunplay in bfs ever, inconsistent, bugged and just outright bad. 
"Staircase" damage fall-off, random spread, limb multiplier, 150ms TTK weapons, drifting reticle (off-center crosshair that follows your barrel and not center of the screen) - all that just makes Netcode worse than what we had in BF4 Beta, mind you, the worst one ever. 

Audio: This thing won "Best Audio Design" at TGA 2025, which btw uses re-used assets from prev games and has really bad enemy step sound, delayed, fully silent and bugged. 

Classes: Assault still stands useless after a year and Support still overpowered. 

Vehicles: omg bruh, when you have a blueprint of something you had already and somehow still make it 10x worse. By far, one of the worst vehicle experience in all Battlefield series, you can't make it worse than this. 
Broken spawns and air resupply

Base AA that fails to stop enemy jets from spawnkilling 
Randoms can block vehicles spawn by just standing there. 
Mini-map is too small for proper navigation.
Glitched out flares 
Laser designators that stay locked for 20 seconds which lol lmao even in BF4 u had to look at enemy to laser tag them and not spam target everything that exists like in bf6. 
Very bad map design for Aircrafts, some maps allow constant spawnkilling FROM an enemy base, some are very limited in map boundaries. 
Air radar, uh it exists, maybe it exists, just maybe. 
Ground vehicle loadouts are another case of schizophrenic upgrades that half of them don't make any sense and some of them just lie to you, doing opposite of what it says in the description. 

Map design: Meh, delusional community asks for "bigger maps" proceeds to never play those "bigger" parts of the map. Nostalgia bait maps are cool, but let's not add BAD nostalgia maps ever again. 
No Spawn screen at the beginning of the match, essentially creating a huge can of worms aka - spawnkilling and ppl krilling themselves to get a vehicle. 

UI: ngl, I'd rather use battlelog. 

Performance: It's somewhat decent BUT if u have 9070XT, consider not buying this game. 

Visual clarity: I hate it, it's too much for my eyes. Not only that this game STILL has epileptic like bugs. 

Aggressive Monetization: I miss when we just had "PREMIUM" and not absolutely useless BF Pro, Battlepass and etc every season. 

Updates & Communication: Great start, though, coms are dead silent since January and updates are really underwhelming, constantly re-introducing previously fixed bugs, being silent on failed CORE mechanics such as TTK, bugged Audio and Visibility issues. 

Pros: parody of BF4 
Cons: parody of BF4 

In conclusion: Happy 1-Year anniversary, buy Battlefield 4.

I think Battlefield 6 is underrated. Mind you, I haven't played the campaign, so my experience is limited to multiplayer. It hasn't tried to shove politics down my throat, talk down to me, or belittle me. I haven't experienced any balancing issues that made me feel like I was being treated unfairly, even when starting from scratch with beginner gear. I can simply pick up the game and play whatever mode I feel like playing.

Every time I play, I have a good time, or at the very least, I'm entertained enough to keep coming back for just one more round. Honestly, I don't understand all the hate. I think the people who worked on this game put a lot of effort into it, and I believe there should be more appreciation for games like this in the industry.

I started with Battlefield 1942 when it was released and purchased both expansion packs, Road to Rome and Secret Weapons. Then I bought Battlefield Vietnam when it came out, and I enjoyed it just as much. Battlefield 2 was another game I purchased on release, and it remains one of my favorites. I remember there was some criticism back then about how you unlocked weapons, so it's not as though complaints about the series are anything new.

I eventually purchased Battlefield: Bad Company 2, although I got it a little later after its release. I loved both the campaign and multiplayer. I skipped Battlefield 3 and Battlefield 4, but I played Battlefield 1 and a bit of Battlefield V. As you can see, I've been around this series for a long time.

That said, I've never considered Battlefield to be some kind of masterpiece franchise where every game needs to be groundbreaking. Even my favorite campaign, Bad Company 2, was great without necessarily redefining storytelling in video games. It didn't need to. Battlefield has always been about playing as an unnamed soldier on a battlefield. You aren't special. You're just another nobody in the middle of a war, and through skill and teamwork, you can help your team climb the scoreboard and achieve victory.

I think some people have unrealistic expectations of what a Battlefield game should be. If you believe Battlefield 6 falls seriously short of its predecessors, I think you might be exaggerating a bit and need to relax. Are there things I don't like about the game? Of course. No game is perfect, and I'm not going to pretend otherwise. But despite its flaws, I still give it a thumbs-up.

I think Battlefield 6 is a solid entry in the series, and I wish more people could appreciate what it gets right instead of focusing so heavily on what they think it gets wrong. A lot of hard work goes into making these games, and I think the people responsible deserve some credit for that.

Maybe we could all stand to be a little less critical sometimes and a little more appreciative of what others bring to the table. Not everything needs to be a masterpiece to be enjoyable or worthwhile.

With over 300 hours played, Battlefield 6 is still my favorite semi-realistic shooter.

While I do think it has less detail and atmosphere compared to classics like Battlefield V or Battlefield 1, the gameplay itself is what keeps me coming back. The gunplay feels great, movement is fluid, and the large-scale battles deliver that unique Battlefield experience that no other franchise quite matches.

One of the things I enjoy the most is the variety of features and playstyles available. Whether I'm focusing on infantry combat, vehicle warfare, squad play, or objective-based teamwork, there's always something exciting happening on the battlefield. The freedom to approach situations in different ways keeps every match feeling fresh, even after hundreds of hours.

Battlefield 1 and Battlefield V may have had more immersion, detail, and atmosphere, but Battlefield 6 has evolved into an incredibly fun and engaging experience. The core gameplay loop is addictive, the action is nonstop, and the moments of chaos and teamwork are exactly why I love this series.

After more than 300 hours, I can confidently say that Battlefield 6 remains my go-to shooter. It may not be perfect, but for me, it's still the best semi-realistic FPS available today.
